cells.label: fact

items.text: Merrill announced the launch of the Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), new services combining automation with portfolio oversight to help clients transition appreciated securities tax-efficiently and deploy cash systematically within the Merrill Lynch Investment Advisory Program.
items.quote: Merrill today announced the launch of Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), new services that combine automation with professional portfolio oversight to help clients simplify asset transitions and cash deployment into managed or custom managed investment strategies in the Merrill Lynch Investment Advisory Program (IAP).

items.text: Merrill created two new kinds of fees for third-party asset managers—data analytics fees and a revenue-sharing 'support fee'—effective January 1, 2027, with data analytics fees ranging from $125,000 to $860,000 per firm per year for actively managed products and $25,000 to $550,000 for passive ETFs.
items.quote: Two kinds of fees have been newly created... Merrill's new data analytics fees will cost asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per-firm, per-year for data on actively managed products... Data on passive ETFs managed through Merrill's platforms will cost between $25,000 and $550,000.
items.unit: data analytics fees per-firm per-year (actively managed products)

items.text: Merrill created a 'negotiable' revenue-sharing 'support fee' for third-party managers costing up to $1 million per $1 billion of funds managed on behalf of Merrill advisors, with fees ranging from 0.02% to a maximum 0.1%.
items.quote: Its new “negotiable” revenue-sharing “support fee” will cost up to $1 million, for every $1 billion of funds an asset manager manages on behalf of Merrill advisors, with fees ranging from 0.02%... to a maximum 0.1%
items.unit: support fee per $1 billion of funds managed

items.text: Merrill executives said in October that the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting after largely pulling back at the end of 2017, with recruited assets to the wealth unit doubling year-over-year.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting. The firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf... restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.

items.text: A Merrill executive indicated the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities, per a conference call with reporters.
items.quote: While the Merrill executive did not mention new AI tools, the message was clear that the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities.
